svg.title: TOPAK H1 — The corpus: layers, precedence, and how a change moves through them
svg.desc: TOPAK is a design corpus in its genesis phase. The checkpoint is the state of record and wins over the narrative; records are immutable after ratification except by typed History rows; the narrative and the glossary are cut with each checkpoint; derived analyses are dated and frozen; specifications, the floor, the reference and the rehearsal are evidence; manifests measure every cut at the commit it measured, and the reference pins what it follows.

text.tspan: The corpus: layers, precedence, and how a change moves through them

svg.text: TOPAK is a design corpus in its genesis phase. The checkpoint is the state of record and wins over the narrative; records are immutable after ratification except by typed History rows; the narrative and the glossary are cut with each checkpoint; derived analyses are dated and frozen; specifications, the floor, the reference and the rehearsal are evidence; manifests measure every cut at the commit it measured, and the reference pins

text.tspan: 1 · Precedence: who wins, who explains, who is evidence, who measures

svg.text: Current: Genesis Checkpoint G9 (2026.10.02, tag G9). Each checkpoint is one cut, never revised: what each record says, what was ratified and by whom, what is owed, what is open, and the manifest that measures it.

Where the narrative and the checkpoint disagree, the checkpoint wins. G9 names ToO revision 12 as standing, not revised at G9, and wins over it where it says every lease the reference issues is rung 0 (items 14, 79); revision 13 is cut against G9 afterwards.
checkpoints/README.md is the 2026.09.30 layout map, the one place stale paths resolve.
ADR-0001 onward, one file each, numbered in the order settled; 45 files to ADR-0046, ADR-0014 reserved.
Never edited after ratification except by a typed History row: an amendment, an erratum, a revision before ratification, or a dependent entry when
decisions/README.md gives status (still headed G8) and is a convenience; the checkpoint is the state of record.
theory-of-operation.md, the head: revision 13 (2026.10.02, tag ToO-rev13), cut against G9; revision 12, against G8, stands at G9 (G9 header). A
revision is an edit, a Changes appendix, a commit and a tag.
glossary.md, revised in place and tagged glossary-<date>; revised twice on 2026.10.02, against G8 and against G9 (tag glossary-2026.10.02b,
owed; a second revision on one date takes a suffix).
revisions/: a closed archive of the dated revisions before the cut (09.10 to rev 9); nothing is added after the cut.
One-shot analyses, reviews and assessments. A derived document is never revised; a new one is written. 21 files in G9's manifest, every one in the
derived index (item 77 closed with G9); new: topak-contain-wrapper-design-2026.10.02.md.
Ten accepted records cite files here by path in their provenance notes, so names do not change.
The 09.17 and 09.26 glossaries stay here, frozen, because records cite them.

text.tspan: 3 · How a change moves through the corpus

svg.text: A record is drafted and revised in place while Proposed: History rows
R1, R2 …, each "Applied — Proposed record, revised in place".
The genesis custodian ratifies under ADR-0029 §2, in numbered
batches (G7: Batches 22–24, one day; G8: Batch 25; G9: Batch 26).
Accepted (genesis); a confirmation-required marker C1–C4 when the
first post-bootstrap quorum must review it (ADR-0029 §4).
Only typed History rows: an amendment (A1 …), an erratum (E1 …),
or a dependent entry (B22 …) when another record's ratification
A dependent entry may change an Annex B row's class (G7 §5). A
pending amendment is marked inline and not applied (G9 §5).
Gn supersedes Gn−1 as the state of record: ratifications, ledger, open
list. tools/cut-manifest.sh cuts SHA256SUMS-Gn under EXCLUDE;
index.tsv gains a row naming the commit; a tag Gn.
The ToO is edited against the checkpoint, with a "Changes from
revision N" appendix, a commit and a tag ToO-revN; the glossary is
revised in place. Until then the checkpoint wins (G9 item 79 owes rev
mechanism/corpus-pins.sha256: the drift test fails when a pinned
record moves; review, bring the code into line or register the
divergence, then replace the pin line.
An ADR-0033 addendum cites the new SHA256SUMS-REF-<date>.

Example, G9 (2026.10.02): ADR-0046 E1, an erratum, ratified alone in Batch 26 (4b417ba) → the launcher built at the reference (c536e21) and its addendum drafted as ADR-0033 A7, pending, citing SHA256SUMS-REF-2026.10.02 (441b56d) → the Run profile drafted as ADR-0034 A2, marked inline and not applied (ec08884) → Run's tools built (c534a42) and ADR-0033 A8 drafted, pending, citing SHA256SUMS-REF-2026.10.02b, with the ADR-0033 pin replaced (66b8e55) →
G9 cut, SHA256SUMS-G9, 392 entries (97a61e8), and its index row (a15f7f1) → ToO revision 13 and the glossary against G9 (9e811bc). SHA256SUMS-G8 fails 14 entries at G9's tree, by construction.

text.tspan: Two kinds of manifest failure that are correct

svg.text: SHA256SUMS-G8 fails 14 entries at G9's tree by construction (ADR-0033 A7, A8, ADR-0034 A2, ADR-0046 E1; the ToO and glossary revised after its cut; nine files under spec/) and verifies 372 of 372 at 1151832 (G9 §9).
SHA256SUMS-REF-2026.10.02b fails two entries at G9's tree, the pin file and the register, which moved after c534a42; 84 of 84 there. -REF-2026.10.02 fails 18; 82 of 82 at c536e21.
Frozen records that cite pre-move paths are not edited: their digests are pinned. Two such citations are knowingly left stale and resolve through the layout map.

text.tspan: Pointers still behind the state of record, as the records say

svg.text: G9's header names revision 12 as the standing narrative; revision 13 is written against G9 afterwards (items 14, 79). ToO-rev13 is made; glossary-2026.10.02b, which the glossary cites, is owed.
mechanism/GAPS-AND-ASSUMPTIONS.md names G9 and revision 12 in its header (item 71, discharged at G9), and decisions/README.md still gives status at G8.
floor/README.md says T_persona is not yet read by the reference; G7 §2.2 says it now is (ADR-0033 A6).
